units.text: Make sure you have specified the file names correctly, either in a context diff header or with an ‘⟦0⟧’ line. Take care to not send out reversed patches, since these make people wonder whether they have already applied the patch.
units.sourceHTML: Make sure you have specified the file names correctly, either in a context diff header or with an ‘Index:’ line. Take care to not send out reversed patches, since these make people wonder whether they have already applied the patch.

units.text: Avoid sending patches that compare backup file names like ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧, since this might confuse ⟦2⟧ into patching a backup file instead of the real file. Instead, send patches that compare the same base file names in different directories, e.g. ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧.
units.sourceHTML: Avoid sending patches that compare backup file names like README.orig or README~, since this might confuse patch into patching a backup file instead of the real file. Instead, send patches that compare the same base file names in different directories, e.g. old/README and new/README.

units.text: To save people from partially applying a patch before other patches that should have gone before it, you can make the first patch in the patch file update a file with a name like ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧, which contains a patch level or version number. If the input file contains the wrong version number, ⟦2⟧ will complain immediately.
units.sourceHTML: To save people from partially applying a patch before other patches that should have gone before it, you can make the first patch in the patch file update a file with a name like patchlevel.h or version.c, which contains a patch level or version number. If the input file contains the wrong version number, patch will complain immediately.

units.text: An even clearer way to prevent this problem is to put a ‘⟦0⟧’ line before the patch. If the leading text in the patch file contains a line that starts with ‘⟦1⟧’, ⟦2⟧ takes the next word from that line (normally a version number) and checks whether the next input file contains that word, preceded and followed by either white space or a newline. If not, ⟦3⟧ prompts you for confirmation before proceeding. This makes it difficult to accidentally apply patches in the wrong order.
units.sourceHTML: An even clearer way to prevent this problem is to put a ‘Prereq:’ line before the patch. If the leading text in the patch file contains a line that starts with ‘Prereq:’, patch takes the next word from that line (normally a version number) and checks whether the next input file contains that word, preceded and followed by either white space or a newline. If not, patch prompts you for confirmation before proceeding. This makes it difficult to accidentally apply patches in the wrong order.
